newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end trade lower lacking impetus.
newsitem.headline: German shares end trade lower lacking impetus.

text.p: German shares end bourse trade lower on Monday as the U.S. Labor Day holiday scuppered hopes of the DAX finding new impetus to forge any new, significant gains.
At the end of bourse trade the DAX index, which gauges trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, was down 10.95 points, or 0.43 percent, at 2,532.88 points.

A slightly firmer dollar helped offset the effect of lower German bonds, but the U.S. currency was still way off its highs of several weeks ago and did not provide any real inspiration in trade generally lacking direction.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG was hit by early selling following a newspaper report on Friday of problems with cars produced at its Wolfsburg plant.
Volkswagen ended down 6.30 marks at 543.70 marks.
Shares in mixed utility Veba AG were boosted at bourse open by reports that it was planning a deal with gas company Ruhrgas on use of Ruhrgas' cable network for Veba's telecoms business.
However, Veba shares ended bourse trade 41 pfennigs lower at 77.24 marks in line with the market.
German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG ended bourse trade 2.20 marks lower at 208.30 marks after German cartel authorities confirmed they were looking into its pricing structure on domestic flights.
